claim: Schmidt, Schneider & Hennig's ICML 2021 large-scale optimizer benchmark (50,000+ runs, 15 optimizers) never reports or computes a formal interaction, ANOVA, factorial, or eta-squared statistic anywhere in its 37-page full text.
stance_target: Gap-4 target position: no prior ML-benchmarking paper reports and interprets a component-by-component interaction term
scope_conditions: Deep-learning optimizer benchmarking literature, 15 optimizers x multiple tasks, ICML 2021
quoted_support: Full-text grep for interaction, ANOVA, analysis of variance, factorial, crossed, eta squared, main effect returned zero hits across all 125,317 characters of extracted PDF text.

claim: The paper's only task-dependence language is qualitative ('Optimizer performance varies greatly across tasks'; 'performance... depends on the problem'), never operationalized as a variance-decomposition or interaction effect size.
scope_conditions: Same paper, findings section and abstract
quoted_support: "Optimizer performance varies greatly across tasks." / "performance highly depends on the problem (see Figure 4)."

claim: The paper explicitly declines to identify a single dominant optimizer across all tasks, instead identifying a reduced competitive subset with Adam remaining a strong contender.
scope_conditions: 15 popular deep learning optimizers, standardized benchmark suite
quoted_support: "While we cannot discern an optimization method clearly dominating across all tested tasks, we identify a significantly reduced subset of specific optimizers and parameter choices that generally lead to competitive results in our experiments: Adam remains a strong contender, with newer methods failing to significantly and consistently outperform it."

claim: Venue for this paper is independently verifiable as ICML 2021 / PMLR 139 directly from a copyright footer embedded in the extracted PDF text, not merely inferred from the submission year.
quoted_support: "Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, 2021. Copyright 2021 by the author(s)."
